sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can add and subtract fractions with different denominators by finding a common denominator.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Adding and subtracting fractions -- To add or subtract fractions with different denominators, we must first find a common denominator so that both fractions have the same-sized parts.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Find the LCM of the denominators, convert each fraction to equivalent fractions, then add or subtract numerators.
&frac{a}{b} + &frac{c}{d} = &frac{ad + bc}{bd}
Cross-multiply to find equivalent numerators

Key examples:
  ✓ &frac{1}{3} + &frac{1}{4} = &frac{7}{12}  (LCM of 3 and 4 is 12)
  ✓ &frac{3}{5} - &frac{1}{3} = &frac{4}{15}  (LCM of 5 and 3 is 15)
  ✓ &frac{2}{3} + &frac{1}{6} = &frac{5}{6}  (LCM of 3 and 6 is 6)
  ✗ &frac{1}{3} + &frac{1}{4} = &frac{2}{7}  (cannot add numerators and denominators)
  ✗ &frac{3}{5} - &frac{1}{3} = &frac{2}{2}  (subtracted both top and bottom)
